albums.blurb: Medeski Martin & Wood are a New York trio — John Medeski on Hammond B-3 organ and keys, Billy Martin on drums, and Chris Wood on bass — who came up through the downtown avant-jazz scene of the early 1990s. Shack-man, their fourth album, was recorded in June 1996 in a remote, solar-powered plywood shack in Hawaii, and it distills their sound into eleven instrumental tracks of simmering soul-jazz and greasy funk grooves; it helped open the door for the wave of instrumental groove bands, like Soulive, that followed on the jam circuit.
albums.reception: The album became the trio's commercial breakthrough, peaking at No. 7 on Billboard's Contemporary Jazz Albums chart.

albums.blurb: PREP are a London four-piece formed in 2015 — singer Tom Havelock, classically trained keyboardist Llywelyn ap Myrddin, drummer Guillaume Jambel, and producer Dan Radclyffe — who built an audience through the EPs Futures and Cold Fire before releasing this self-titled debut full-length on Bright Antenna Records in October 2020. It polishes their blend of late-'70s and early-'80s soft rock, city pop, and contemporary R&B, with contributions from rapper-singer Miso, saxophonist Mike Lesirge, and a 16-piece string orchestra.
albums.reception: The Line of Best Fit described the album as “a much-needed funk-fueled trip to a sun-filled beach,” and it drew radio support from BBC Radio 1, KCRW, and Beats 1.

albums.blurb: Rosalía is a Catalan singer who spent years training in traditional flamenco cante before making this second album, which began as her thesis project at the Catalonia College of Music and was co-produced with El Guincho. A concept record loosely following Flamenca, an anonymous 13th-century Occitan novel, it sets flamenco's handclaps and melisma inside stark modern R&B and electronic production, marking her leap from the acoustic traditionalism of her 2017 debut Los Ángeles to international stardom.
albums.reception: It won Album of the Year at the 2019 Latin Grammy Awards — where it also took Best Contemporary Pop Vocal Album — making Rosalía the first woman to win the top prize since Shakira in 2006.
